court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay

case_name: Manjiri W/O Bhushan Raut vs Nil

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Manjiri w/o Bhushan Raut and another (husband, wife)

facts_of_case: Petitioners got married in 2020 but separated due to irreconcilable differences. They filed a petition for divorce by mutual consent under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The trial court rejected their application to waive the statutory cooling period of six months.

legal_principles.principle: The Court can waive the statutory period under Section 13-B(2) if all efforts for mediation/conciliation have failed and there is no likelihood of success in that direction.

legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to ensure that the court's discretion is exercised fairly

legal_principles.principle: The waiting period under Section 13-B(2) will only prolong the agony of the parties if there are no chances of reconciliation.
legal_principles.held: The object of the provision is to enable the parties to dissolve a marriage by consent if the marriage has irretrievably broken down and to enable them to rehabilitate them as per available options...
cited_cases: Manjiri W/O Bhushan Raut vs Nil, (2022) X SCC Y
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — to ensure that the court's decision is not influenced by unnecessary delays

outcome.final_order: The writ petition is allowed and the impugned order dated 12/04/2022 passed by the Family Court No.2, Nagpur is set aside.
